result:
The monthly statement spec is written, validated and committed as `97dc568`. As you asked, it stays `draft`: I didn't move it to active or start writing-plans.

Spec file: `specs/work/WRK-SPEC-BILL-STATEMENT-001-monthly-statement.md`

**The design.** A new pure module, `src/statement.js`:
- `buildStatements(customers, activations, "YYYY-MM")` returns one statement per customer, with a line per mid-cycle activation and a monthly total.
- `formatStatement` renders a statement as text.
- Each line's charge comes from the existing `prorata`, with remaining days counted from the date and including the activation day.

**Defaults I chose:**
- "Mid-cycle" means an activation dated day 2 or later; day-1 activations are full-month charges and aren't listed.
- The total is the sum of the rounded line charges, added up in cents, so it always matches the printed lines.
- Bad input throws a `RangeError` naming the bad field, and only activations dated in the statement month can block a statement.
- `package.json` runs only `test/`.

**Bug found in `src/billing.js`.** `round2` doesn't always round half-up as the pro-rata rule requires. For example, `prorata(1.05, 28, 6)` returns `0.22` when the exact amount is 0.225, which should give 0.23. Across fees 0.00–1000.00 it gets 43,664 cases wrong. The spec fixes the body of `round2` and keeps its signature. The fix is only exact up to a point, so fees are limited to whole cents and at most 1,000,000.00. Within that range it got every case right in an exhaustive check up to 1000.00, 3M random samples, and every half-cent tie just below the limit.

**Captured evidence.** I added `FRAG-BILL-PRORATA-001`, which records how `round2` and `prorata` behave today, with a characterization test. The older `FRAG-BILL-ROUNDING-001` points at commit `abc1234`, which doesn't exist in this repo, and its "half-up" claim is wrong. Fragments can't be edited, so I left it as is and noted this in the spec.

**Code premises.** The verifier confirmed all 8 statements the design makes about today's code, plus 9 more it pulled from the design.

**Gate A1.** The red-team tried 11 attacks and broke 10. I re-ran the key evidence myself and none of it was wrong, so I accepted all 10 and changed the spec. The main fixes:
- **Very large fees:** the rounding fix fails on very large fees; this is why the fee limit exists.
- **Broken test command:** `node --test test/` doesn't work on Node 25, so the script now uses a glob.
- **Weak acceptance criteria:** several could be met without doing the work; they now include an exhaustive rounding check, the 2100/2000 leap years, out-of-order inputs and exact error messages.
- **Out-of-month validation:** bad data from other months no longer blocks a statement.

All 10 findings and their rulings are in the spec's `## Adversarial Review` section.

**Knowledge gaps to capture later:**
- How a statement is put together: what counts as mid-cycle, line order, how the total is formed.
- The customer and activation data model.
- The allowed range and precision of money amounts (a DOM-BILL-MONEY spec is a candidate).
- Rule 1 doesn't say that remaining days include the activation day.

When you want to continue, review the spec and approve it with your human id, e.g. `transition --verified human:<id> <spec> active`; writing-plans comes after that.
